papers.title: Nutrient control enables metabolic reconstruction of Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus GG and analysis of secretions.
papers.abstract: Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus GG (LGG) is an important gut commensal bacterial strain that has been extensively studied in both industrial and health settings. Despite its long history of study, a high-quality genome-scale metabolic network model (GEM) for LGG has yet to be reconstructed. Only automatically generated draft models have been published, which have notoriously limited functional accuracy. Furthermore, comprehensive nutrient requirements have not been established for well-controlled in vitro studies. Here, we present the first curated GEM for LGG using a new approach for reconstruct
papers.summary: The authors present the first manually curated genome-scale metabolic model for the probiotic gut bacterium Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus GG, built using a new reconstruction approach and informed by experimentally determined nutrient requirements. They also establish defined nutrient conditions for controlled in vitro growth studies and analyze the strain's secreted metabolites. This provides a more accurate computational and experimental foundation for studying LGG metabolism.

papers.title: Phylogenomics, spatiotemporal transcriptional dynamics and Cis-regulatory architecture underlying the Portulaca oleracea antioxidant network under extreme salinity.
papers.abstract: Global soil salinization severely threatens agricultural productivity. Portulaca oleracea L., an extreme xerohalophyte, displays exceptional salinity tolerance, yet the transcriptional architecture coordinating its antioxidant defenses across organs and developmental stages remains unresolved. In this study, multi-tissue high-throughput RNA-Seq, quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) validation, comparative phylogenomics across 154 plant genomes, and condition-specific gene regulatory network (GRN) modeling were integrated to characterize 436 antioxidant loci in P. oleracea. Under chronic hypers
papers.journal: Plant science : an international journal of experimental plant biology
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-tissue RNA-Seq, qRT-PCR, comparative phylogenomics across 154 plant genomes, and condition-specific gene regulatory network modeling to characterize 436 antioxidant loci in the extreme halophyte Portulaca oleracea under chronic hypersalinity. It reveals spatiotemporal transcriptional dynamics and cis-regulatory architecture coordinating antioxidant defenses across organs and developmental stages, providing a framework for understanding salinity tolerance in this xerohalophyte.

papers.title: Temporal multi-omics reveals regulatory transitions and renoprotective candidates in cisplatin-induced kidney injury.
papers.abstract: Cisplatin is a classic first-line platinum drug extensively used in chemotherapy for solid tumors, yet its clinical applications are limited by dose-dependent nephrotoxicity. The dynamic molecular mechanisms underlying cisplatin-induced kidney injury and regeneration remain incompletely understood. Here, we established two complementary mouse models, a single high-dose cisplatin (SHDC) model and a repeated low-dose cisplatin (RLDC) model, to recapitulate acute and progressive/persistent patterns of renal injury, respectively. Integrated transcriptomic and proteomic analyses reveal temporal tra
papers.summary: This study uses two mouse models of cisplatin-induced kidney injury (single high-dose and repeated low-dose) to profile transcriptomic and proteomic changes over time. The integrated multi-omics analysis reveals dynamic regulatory transitions during injury and regeneration and identifies candidate renoprotective factors. The work provides a temporal molecular map of cisplatin nephrotoxicity that may guide protective strategies.

papers.title: Let there be multifunctionality: Uncovering the dynamical zoo of the AC-DC genetic circuit.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory networks (GRNs) govern many cell processes. While multistability and oscillations are common GRN dynamics, they are typically studied and engineered in isolation. Here, we challenge this separation using the AC-DC circuit, a minimal three-gene network that merges the classical toggle switch and repressilator. Using a thermodynamic formalism and Bayesian inference, we show that a single-inducer version of the circuit displays diverse multifunctional dynamics, including coexistence of oscillations and multistability. We explore robustness, classify emergent behaviors, and analyze
papers.summary: This study analyzes the AC-DC genetic circuit, a minimal three-gene network combining a toggle switch and a repressilator, and shows that a single-inducer version can exhibit multiple dynamical behaviors simultaneously, including coexisting oscillations and multistability. Using thermodynamic modeling and Bayesian inference, the authors map out a diverse 'zoo' of dynamical regimes and assess their robustness. The work challenges the traditional separation of multistability and oscillations in gene regulatory network studies.

papers.title: Robust identification of cell-cell communication heterogeneity in single cells.
papers.abstract: Cell-cell communication modulates cell fate decisions by relaying information across tissues and inducing intracellular responses mediated by gene regulatory networks. Although the inference of cell-cell communication from high-throughput data is gaining popularity, studying how communication pathways operate across biological scales and influence cell fate decisions remains challenging. Here, we present scRICH (robust identification of cell-cell communication heterogeneity in single cells), a computational framework that leverages single-cell and spatial transcriptomics data to unravel the he
papers.summary: The paper introduces scRICH, a computational framework for inferring cell-cell communication from single-cell and spatial transcriptomics data. It aims to robustly identify heterogeneity in communication pathways across cells and link these signals to downstream gene regulatory effects and cell fate decisions. The method addresses the challenge of studying how communication operates across biological scales.

papers.title: Revisiting Ehrlich carcinoma in the era of precision oncology: bridging classical models with modern systems biology.
papers.abstract: Ehrlich carcinoma (EC) and its ascitic form, Ehrlich ascites carcinoma (EAC), are among the oldest and most widely used experimental tumor models in cancer research. Although they have traditionally been used for anticancer drug screening, their potential to address broader aspects of aggressive tumor biology has received comparatively less attention. EC/EAC exhibits several characteristics associated with advanced malignancy, including rapid tumor growth, angiogenesis, immune dysregulation, metabolic changes, therapeutic resistance, and complex interactions between the tumor and host. These f
papers.summary: This review argues that Ehrlich carcinoma and its ascitic form, despite being among the oldest experimental tumor models, remain underused for studying aggressive tumor biology beyond simple drug screening. The authors highlight how EC/EAC captures features of advanced malignancy—rapid growth, angiogenesis, immune dysregulation, metabolic reprogramming, therapeutic resistance, and tumor-host interactions—and propose integrating it with modern systems biology and precision oncology approaches.

papers.title: Host-like temperature unlocks glucose uptake and metabolism in pathogenic Leptospira.
papers.abstract: Pathogenic Leptospira transitions between environmental reservoirs and mammalian hosts, exposing the bacterium to distinct temperature conditions. Although Leptospira is generally considered to rely primarily on long-chain fatty acids for growth and to have limited capacity to use glucose, whether host-like temperature alters glucose-associated metabolic capacity remains unclear. Here, we used transcriptome-integrated genome-scale metabolic modeling to examine temperature-dependent metabolic states in pathogenic Leptospira. Models contextualized with transcriptomic data from cultures at 37°C p
papers.summary: Using transcriptome-integrated genome-scale metabolic modeling, the authors show that pathogenic Leptospira grown at host-like temperature (37°C) upregulates glucose uptake and metabolism, contrary to the long-held view that this pathogen relies mainly on fatty acids and has limited glucose use. This temperature-dependent metabolic shift may be important for survival and virulence within mammalian hosts.

papers.title: Uncovering combination therapies for immune-mediated inflammatory diseases through systems biology analysis on longitudinal patient data.
papers.abstract: While targeted therapies have reshaped the clinical management of immune-mediated inflammatory diseases (IMIDs), primary non-response remains a major obstacle for many patients. Combining two targeted therapies is an emerging strategy to overcome this therapeutic ceiling, but the number of possible drug pairs makes prioritization difficult. For this objective, we present mitigation of non-response signature (MNRS), a computational approach that uses longitudinal blood transcriptomic data from six IMIDs treated with different targeted therapies to identify the most promising drug combinations.
papers.summary: The authors introduce MNRS, a computational method that uses longitudinal blood transcriptomic data from patients with six immune-mediated inflammatory diseases to prioritize combination therapies that could overcome primary non-response to targeted drugs. By identifying drug pairs that mitigate non-response signatures, the approach narrows the vast space of possible combinations to the most promising candidates.

papers.title: Modeling microbiome modulation of tumor metabolic networks to predict synergistic therapies.
papers.abstract: Differences in microbiome composition profoundly influence drug response, yet methods to model the metabolic impact of microbes on host cells and therapeutics remain limited. We present a microbiome-aware computational framework combining machine learning and genome-scale metabolic models to predict combination therapies for colorectal cancer (CRC) in the presence of Fusobacterium nucleatum (Fn) and other pathogenic, probiotic, and commensal microbes. The model learned predictive metabolic flux signatures from 6,514 drug combination profiles in CRC cell lines and predicted synergistic drug com
papers.summary: The authors present a computational framework that combines machine learning with genome-scale metabolic models to predict how gut microbes, particularly Fusobacterium nucleatum, alter tumor metabolism and drug response in colorectal cancer. Trained on 6,514 drug combination profiles, the model identifies metabolic flux signatures that predict synergistic combination therapies in the presence of different microbial communities. This provides a new approach for incorporating microbiome context into cancer therapy prediction.

papers.title: Donor-Resolved Analysis of HES1-Associated Fibroblast States in Systemic Sclerosis.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: We examined HES1-associated fibroblast states in systemic sclerosis (SSc) and the rationale for testing upstream γ-secretase inhibition with nirogacestat. Methods: We analysed 325,636 skin cells from 230 donors across five non-redundant cohorts using complete computational transcription-factor screens, donor-level activity and trajectory analyses, multiome data and spatial assays. Donors or independent simulations were the inference units, with cohort adjustment and multiplicity correction where applicable. Three independent 200 ns molecular dynamics runs per condition c
papers.summary: This study analyzed over 325,000 skin cells from 230 donors across five cohorts to characterize HES1-associated fibroblast states in systemic sclerosis (SSc), using transcription-factor screens, donor-level activity and trajectory analyses, multiome data, and spatial assays. The authors provide a rationale for testing upstream γ-secretase inhibition with nirogacestat as a therapeutic strategy targeting these fibroblast states. Molecular dynamics simulations were used to support the mechanistic interpretation.

papers.title: Metabolic modeling with reverse mapping links host perturbations to Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
papers.abstract: Understanding host-pathogen interactions during Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) infection has largely relied on identifying bacterial genes essential for intracellular survival. However, conventional reverse genetics approaches often overlook host pathways that regulate Mtb growth. Here, we developed a backtracing strategy to link host metabolic modulators with specific Mtb proteins. A genome-scale host metabolic model integrated with lung transcriptomic data from H37Rv-infected mice predicted 18 host proteins essential for Mtb survival. We validated this through pharmacological inhibition, s
papers.summary: The authors developed a computational 'backtracing' strategy that integrates a genome-scale host metabolic model with lung transcriptomic data from Mtb-infected mice to predict host proteins whose metabolic activity supports bacterial survival. They identified 18 candidate host proteins and validated them pharmacologically, showing that host metabolic perturbations can be linked to specific Mtb proteins. This reframes host-pathogen interaction studies by highlighting host metabolic dependencies rather than only bacterial essential genes.

papers.title: Single-cell transcriptomic analysis reveals autophagy-associated transcriptional vulnerability of dopaminergic neurons after atrazine exposure.
papers.abstract: Atrazine (ATZ) is a widely used triazine herbicide with potential neurotoxic effects, but the cell-type-specific responses of midbrain dopaminergic neurons to ATZ exposure remain poorly defined. In this study, we applied single-cell RNA sequencing to midbrain tissues from adult male mice exposed to ATZ for 28 days (a sub-acute exposure) to characterize transcriptional alterations associated with dopaminergic neuronal injury. Three mice per group were used for scRNA-seq, and group comparisons were performed using one-way ANOVA followed by Tukey's post hoc test, or the Kruskal-Wallis test with D
papers.summary: This study used single-cell RNA sequencing of mouse midbrain after 28 days of atrazine exposure to map cell-type-specific transcriptional changes, focusing on dopaminergic neurons. The authors identify an autophagy-associated transcriptional signature that may render dopaminergic neurons vulnerable to atrazine-induced injury. The work provides a cell-resolved view of herbicide neurotoxicity in a Parkinson's-relevant neuronal population.

papers.title: Integrative analysis of Alzheimer's disease molecular networks with circadian regulators for prioritization of drug repurposing candidates.
papers.abstract: BackgroundAlzheimer's disease (AD) is a multifactorial neurodegenerative disorder characterized by complex molecular mechanisms. Growing evidence indicates that circadian rhythm disruption contributes to disease progression and interacts with pathogenic pathways. Although multi-omics resources, compound perturbation profiles, and pharmacological bioactivity data are increasingly available, their integrative use for drug repurposing prioritization in AD, particularly with explicit consideration of circadian rhythm, remains limited.ObjectiveThis study aimed to prioritize drug repurposing candida
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics Alzheimer's disease molecular networks with circadian rhythm regulators to prioritize drug repurposing candidates. By combining compound perturbation profiles and pharmacological bioactivity data, the authors identify existing drugs that may target AD-relevant pathways influenced by circadian disruption. The work highlights circadian biology as an underused axis for computational drug repurposing in neurodegeneration.

papers.title: MetworkPy: A Python Package for Graph- and Information-theoretic Investigation of Metabolic Networks.
papers.abstract: Metabolism plays an important role in physiology and disease. In silico Genome-Scale Metabolic Models (GSMMs) are useful for informing analysis of metabolism and contextualizing high-throughput molecular profiling data. Flux balance analysis (FBA) based approaches can use GSMMs to predict metabolic reaction flux states and condition-specific alterations, but most FBA methods are limited by: 1) needing metabolic objective functions that are difficult to define experimentally, and 2) confining comparisons to extrema of reaction flux distributions.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: MetworkPy is a new Python package that analyzes genome-scale metabolic models using graph theory and information theory, avoiding the need for predefined metabolic objective functions that constrain traditional flux balance analysis. It enables comparison of full reaction flux distributions rather than just their extremes, providing a more flexible framework for contextualizing metabolic profiling data.

papers.title: Gene Regulatory Network Reconstruction to Decipher the Molecular Mechanisms Governing Bacteriocyte-Based Symbioses.
papers.abstract: Intracellular bacteria with beneficial roles for their hosts are present in more than 10% of all insect species. In intracellular nutritional symbioses, these symbionts are typically confined to specialized host cells known as bacteriocytes. Bacteriocytes are remarkable novel cells that arose independently and repeatedly across multiple insect lineages. They are fascinating structures, yet the molecular mechanisms regulating their development, function and even their evolutionary origins, remain largely unknown. Nonetheless, an important role for certain transcription factors in development an
papers.summary: This review discusses how gene regulatory network (GRN) reconstruction can be used to understand the molecular mechanisms underlying bacteriocyte-based nutritional symbioses in insects. Bacteriocytes are specialized host cells that house beneficial intracellular bacteria and have evolved independently many times, yet their development and function remain poorly understood. The authors highlight the role of transcription factors and argue that GRN approaches can reveal how these novel cell types arise and operate.

papers.title: Whole-cell spatiotemporal model and multimodal data illuminate the multiscale light responses in a photosynthetic bacterium.
papers.abstract: Photosynthetic microorganisms rely on multiple central carbon metabolism pathways to adapt to fluctuating light and energy availability across diel cycles. Mechanistic insight into the regulatory dynamics of this adaptation requires integrating processes that operate across disparate timescales, from rapid redox-dependent post-translational modifications (PTMs) to slower changes in protein expression and metabolic pathway usage. Here, we develop a whole-cell 4D (3D + time) model of the marine cyanobacterium Prochlorococcus marinus MED4 that explicitly represents the spatial, subcellular organi
papers.summary: The authors built a whole-cell 4D (3D + time) computational model of the marine cyanobacterium Prochlorococcus marinus MED4 that integrates spatial subcellular organization with regulatory dynamics across timescales, from fast redox-dependent post-translational modifications to slower protein expression and metabolic pathway shifts. Combined with multimodal data, the model illuminates how this photosynthetic bacterium coordinates multiscale responses to fluctuating light. This provides a mechanistic framework for understanding light adaptation in a key marine primary producer.

papers.title: Homeostatic Correction During Severe Physiologic Stress: A Phase-Specific Model for GC-GRα-Coordinated Organism-Wide Adaptation.
papers.abstract: Critical illness is increasingly recognized as a disorder of disrupted systemic homeostasis rather than simply a consequence of maladaptive systemic inflammation or isolated organ failure. Although researchers have extensively investigated adaptive biologic responses to severe physiologic stress, far less attention has been paid to the integrative mechanisms that coordinate these responses across multiple organ systems throughout the course of illness. This review synthesizes current evidence from systems biology, immunology, endocrinology, network physiology, and critical care to present a sy
papers.summary: This review proposes a phase-specific model in which glucocorticoids and the glucocorticoid receptor alpha (GC-GRα) coordinate organism-wide homeostatic correction during severe physiologic stress, reframing critical illness as a disorder of disrupted systemic homeostasis rather than merely maladaptive inflammation or isolated organ failure. It synthesizes evidence from systems biology, immunology, endocrinology, network physiology, and critical care to describe how adaptive responses are integrated across organ systems over the course of illness.

papers.title: CardamomOT: A mechanistic optimal transport-based framework for gene regulatory network inference, trajectory reconstruction and generative modeling.
papers.abstract: A key challenge in inferring gene regulatory networks (GRNs) governing cellular processes such as differentiation and reprogramming from experimental data lies in the impossibility of directly measuring protein dynamics at the single-cell level, which prevents establishing causal relationships between regulator activity and target responses. In earlier work, we introduced CARDAMOM, an algorithm that uses temporal snapshots of scRNA-seq data to calibrate a GRN-driven mechanistic model of gene expression. However, this method had several limitations: it could only rely on the relative ordering o
papers.summary: CardamomOT extends the CARDAMOM algorithm into a mechanistic optimal transport framework that infers gene regulatory networks from single-cell RNA-seq data without requiring precise temporal ordering of snapshots. It jointly performs GRN inference, trajectory reconstruction, and generative modeling of cellular dynamics, addressing limitations of the original method that relied on relative ordering of time points. This provides a more flexible and principled approach for studying differentiation and reprogramming from snapshot data.

papers.title: Protamine gene expression is associated with sperm motility in rams: An integrative experimental and gene network analysis.
papers.abstract: Protamine 1 (PRM1) and protamine 2 (PRM2) are essential regulators of sperm chromatin condensation and genome integrity, and their dysregulation has been associated with impaired male fertility. However, their role in rams remains insufficiently characterized. This study investigated the relationship between protamine gene expression and semen quality in rams and explored their potential upstream regulatory mechanisms using gene regulatory network (GRN) analysis. Fifteen ejaculates from five rams were analyzed. Based on total sperm motility using computer-assisted sperm analysis (CASA), ejacul
papers.summary: This study examined whether expression levels of protamine genes PRM1 and PRM2 correlate with semen quality in rams, using CASA-based motility measurements across ejaculates from five animals. The authors combined experimental expression data with gene regulatory network analysis to identify potential upstream regulators of protamine expression. The work suggests protamine gene expression is associated with sperm motility in rams, extending findings from other species to this livestock context.

papers.title: Disagreement-informed arbitration for gene regulatory network inference: A score-level meta-classifier and a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflict.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory network inference methods routinely disagree about individual edges, and practitioners resolve those conflicts by choosing one method or averaging them all. We ask whether the conflict can instead be arbitrated per edge. A gradient-boosted classifier is trained on the raw scores that ten inference methods-correlation-based, information-theoretic, sparse-regression and tree-ensemble, including GENIE3, GRNBoost2, CLR and ARACNe-assign to each candidate regulator-target pair, so that the weight given to each method varies from edge to edge. Across six single-cell perturbation scre
papers.summary: The authors propose a per-edge arbitration approach for gene regulatory network inference, training a gradient-boosted meta-classifier on the raw scores from ten different inference methods so that method weighting varies for each candidate regulator-target pair rather than using a single method or simple averaging. They also develop a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflicts, evaluated across six single-cell perturbation screens. This reframes method disagreement as a signal to be exploited rather than a nuisance to be resolved by consensus.

papers.title: Comparative phylogenomics and transcriptional regulatory networks of AQPs, HSPs, and LEA proteins in salt-stressed Portulaca oleracea.
papers.abstract: Soil salinization severely threatens global food security, necessitating systematic investigations of halophytes like Portulaca oleracea to decode the molecular mechanisms of environmental resilience. Utilizing an integrated framework of deep learning-based genome annotation (58,817 predicted genes; 96.5% BUSCO completeness), multi-tissue RNA-Seq, phylogenomics, and gene regulatory network (GRN) inference, the synergistic orchestration of 78 aquaporins (AQPs), 525 heat shock proteins (HSPs), and 119 late embryogenesis abundant (LEA) proteins was elucidated. The active transcriptome, encompassi
papers.journal: Plant science : an international journal of experimental plant biology
papers.summary: This study combines deep learning-based genome annotation, multi-tissue RNA-Seq, phylogenomics, and gene regulatory network inference to characterize aquaporins, heat shock proteins, and LEA proteins in the halophyte Portulaca oleracea under salt stress. The authors report a high-quality annotated genome (58,817 genes, 96.5% BUSCO completeness) and reveal coordinated transcriptional regulation of these stress-responsive gene families. The work provides a resource for understanding salt tolerance mechanisms in halophytes.

papers.title: A metabolic model based on a pangenome core reveals putative conserved biochemical features of the phytopathogen Xylella fastidiosa.
papers.abstract: Xylella fastidiosa is a xylem-limited phytopathogenic bacterium responsible for severe diseases in many economically important crops. Despite its impact, its metabolism remains poorly characterized due to fastidious growth and the limited availability of defined culture media. Here, we reconstruct the first pangenome-based genome-scale metabolic model for X. fastidiosa, integrating conserved metabolic functions from 18 strains across five subspecies. The resulting consensus model, iXfcore, is manually curated and used to explore the species' metabolic capabilities. Model simulations predict mi
papers.summary: Researchers built the first pangenome-based genome-scale metabolic model for the plant pathogen Xylella fastidiosa, integrating conserved metabolic functions from 18 strains across five subspecies. The manually curated consensus model, iXfcore, was used to predict metabolic capabilities and identify putative conserved biochemical features of this poorly characterized, fastidious bacterium.

papers.title: Hybrid genome‑scale metabolic modeling and machine learning reveal cost‑efficient strategies for phototrophic polyhydroxybutyrate production in Rhodopseudomonas palustris.
papers.abstract: Plastic pollution from fossil-based materials is a major global environmental challenge. Microbially derived bioplastics, such as polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB), offer a promising biodegradable alternative. However, the high substrate and operational costs of PHB production remain a major barrier to large-scale deployment. Optimizing PHB synthesis requires navigating a multidimensional design space of metabolic, nutritional, and operational variables, which is impractical to explore experimentally. This study presents an integrated computational framework that combines a genome-scale metabolic mode
papers.summary: This study combines a genome-scale metabolic model of Rhodopseudomonas palustris with machine learning to explore the design space for phototrophic polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB) production. The hybrid framework identifies cost-efficient combinations of metabolic, nutritional, and operational variables that improve PHB yields, avoiding impractical exhaustive experimental screening. It offers a computational strategy to guide strain and process optimization for biodegradable bioplastic production.

papers.title: Causality analysis of toxicological mechanisms in networked systems such as adverse outcome pathway networks.
papers.abstract: This paper examines why robust causality assessment is central to toxicology yet increasingly difficult in networked biological systems, including Adverse Outcome Pathway (AOP) networks and multi-omics datasets. Classical causal frameworks (e.g., Koch/Dale reasoning and Bradford Hill-type considerations) remain useful for scoping, but they offer limited operational guidance for multifactorial, nonlinear, and feedback-dominated mechanisms. We therefore synthesize a modern toolbox for causality analysis in toxicology spanning directed acyclic graphs for explicit causal assumptions, quantitative
papers.summary: This review argues that traditional causality frameworks like Koch's postulates and Bradford Hill criteria are insufficient for toxicology's increasingly networked, multifactorial systems such as Adverse Outcome Pathway networks and multi-omics data. It synthesizes a modern causality toolbox—including directed acyclic graphs for making causal assumptions explicit and quantitative methods—to guide mechanistic interpretation in these complex settings. The paper is a conceptual and methodological primer rather than a primary study.

papers.title: Proteomics and network biology insights into inflammation suppression during prolonged high-altitude hypoxia acclimatization.
papers.abstract: For decades, the study of high-altitude acclimatization has been a vital area of scientific inquiry aimed at enhancing human resilience, particularly in the context of military deployments. While most existing research has focused on acute inflammatory responses to hypoxia, limited information is available on the molecular mechanisms underlying long-term high-altitude acclimatization. To address this gap, the present study investigated the plasma proteomic alterations associated with 120 days of high-altitude exposure at 14,500 ft by employing quantitative proteomics combined with computationa
papers.summary: This study used quantitative plasma proteomics combined with computational network analysis to profile molecular changes during 120 days of acclimatization to high altitude (14,500 ft). The key finding is that prolonged hypoxia exposure is associated with suppression of inflammatory pathways, contrasting with the acute inflammatory responses typically reported in short-term hypoxia studies. The work provides proteomic and network-level insights into how the body adapts to chronic high-altitude conditions.

papers.title: Population-specific transcriptomic shifts underlie secondary metabolic diversification in Aspergillus flavus Link and the domestication of Aspergillus oryzae (Ahlb.).
papers.abstract: The genomic signatures of microbial domestication remain poorly understood within the context of natural population variation. Here, we demonstrate that Aspergillus oryzae, the filamentous fungus used in soy sauce and sake production, shares more recent ancestry with a predominantly northern, largely non-aflatoxigenic population of Aspergillus flavus (population C). A. oryzae isolates also overlap with the recently described, clinically enriched A. flavus population D, suggesting multiple domestication events. All isolates tested retained pathogenicity in a zebrafish infection model. At the tr
papers.summary: This study shows that the domesticated fungus Aspergillus oryzae, used in soy sauce and sake production, shares recent ancestry with a specific northern population of the wild fungus A. flavus that largely lacks aflatoxin production, and also overlaps with a clinically enriched population, suggesting multiple domestication events. All tested isolates remained pathogenic in a zebrafish infection model, and population-specific transcriptomic shifts underlie diversification of secondary metabolism. The work links natural population variation to microbial domestication signatures.

papers.title: GP-DHT: A dual-head transformer with supervised contrastive learning for shared-gene pretraining and single-cell GRN prediction.
papers.abstract: Gene Regulatory Networks (GRNs) are crucial for understanding cell fate decisions and disease mechanisms. However, inferring GRNs from single-cell RNA sequencing remains challenging due to noise, data sparsity, and species-specific distribution variations. We propose GP-DHT (Gene Pair-Dual Head Transformer), a single-cell GRN inference framework that pre-trains gene representations on a unified shared gene space using the BEELINE datasets of humans and mice. It models gene-cell expression relationships through a multi-relational heterograph and predicts transcription factor (TF)-target regulat
papers.summary: GP-DHT is a dual-head transformer framework that pre-trains gene representations on a unified shared-gene space across human and mouse BEELINE datasets, using supervised contrastive learning and a multi-relational heterograph to model gene-cell expression relationships. It then predicts transcription factor-target regulatory interactions for single-cell GRN inference, aiming to overcome noise, sparsity, and species-specific distribution shifts.

papers.title: An experimentally validated manually curated genome-scale metabolic model of Enterococcus faecium TX0016 reproduces high-throughput phenotyping data.
papers.abstract: Enterococci are Gram-positive opportunistic pathogens responsible for a wide range of nosocomial infections. One enterococcal species, Enterococcus faecium, is steadily increasing in prevalence and has been listed among major multidrug-resistant ESKAPE pathogens. To gain systems-level insights into its metabolism and support discovery of potential therapeutic targets, we constructed iDR478, a comprehensive manually curated genome-scale metabolic model (GEM) for E. faecium TX0016 (strain DO). The reconstruction was based on extensive homology searches and literature evidence, and was further re
papers.summary: The authors constructed iDR478, a manually curated genome-scale metabolic model for the multidrug-resistant pathogen Enterococcus faecium TX0016, built from homology searches and literature evidence. The model was experimentally validated and reproduces high-throughput phenotyping data, providing a systems-level platform for studying its metabolism and identifying potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Targeting the gut-tumor axis: probiotic therapy as an adjunct strategy in colorectal cancer treatment.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a multifactorial disease driven by interactions among host genetics, immune dysregulation, environmental factors, and gut microbiota. The gut-tumor axis regulates CRC progression through inflammatory signaling, oxidative stress, epithelial barrier disruption, and immune imbalance. Probiotic-derived metabolites act as bioactive molecules capable of restoring host-microbiome homeostasis and modulating tumor-associated pathways.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This review examines how the gut-tumor axis drives colorectal cancer progression through inflammation, oxidative stress, barrier disruption, and immune imbalance, and how probiotic-derived metabolites can counteract these mechanisms. It positions probiotic therapy as an adjunct strategy for restoring host-microbiome homeostasis and modulating tumor-associated pathways in CRC treatment.

papers.title: Towards epigenetically informed and biobank-driven precision immunotherapy in melanoma.
papers.abstract: Cutaneous melanoma (CM) is a highly immunogenic and therapeutically intricate solid tumor, exemplifying the interactions between tumors and the immune system. Despite the significant enhancement in survival rates for patients with advanced melanoma due to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), numerous patients either exhibit resistance to these agents or develop immune evasion mechanisms. This underscores the pressing necessity to identify biological determinants of drug responses. A significant body of research indicates that epigenetic alterations, including DNA methylation, histone modificat
papers.summary: This review discusses how epigenetic changes such as DNA methylation and histone modifications influence melanoma's response to immune checkpoint inhibitors, and argues that integrating epigenetic data with large biobank resources could enable more precise immunotherapy selection. It highlights the need to identify biological determinants of drug resistance and immune evasion to guide treatment decisions.
